key_insight: This study will compare multiple large language models against clinician-generated benchmark responses on realistic primary-care vignettes in Kenya, Malawi, and Tanzania.
clinical_relevance: It is designed to assess whether LLMs can provide safe, context-appropriate decision support for low-resource primary healthcare settings.
method: Experienced clinicians create 200–250 hypothetical vignettes per country and write benchmark care plans.
Six open-source and proprietary LLMs are prompted with the same vignettes.
Masked expert reviewers compare LLM and human answers on soundness, safety, contextual fit, clarity, completeness, and confidence.
evidence_signal: The protocol uses fully crossed repeated-measures comparisons with at least 358 evaluations per LLM per country, enabling structured expert adjudication rather than direct patient testing.
watch_item: Because the study uses hypothetical vignettes and expert ratings, real-world performance, workflow fit, and patient outcome impact may differ from benchmark results.
paper_title: Evaluating large language models as clinical decision support tools in primary healthcare settings: Protocol for a multi-country comparative validation study on expert-adjudicated hypothetical vignettes (hypMOOVE-PHC)
